newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Prices down on ample prompt supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Prices down on ample prompt supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices fell on Tuesday, weighed down by prompt supplies amid an absence of buyers, traders said on Tuesday.
Prices had found support late last week and Monday after more than a 20-percent slump in value. However, ample supply was once again knocking prices, traders said.
Cst 180-cargoes were offered at $99 per tonne for loading in February in Singapore against no bids. On Monday, quotes were at $98/$100 per tonne.
Traders said supplies in February were ample.
"Kuwait is exporting more than its usual volumes and we see Mideast bunker players bringing supplies here," said a trader.
The Fujairah bunker market was seen slightly softer with more than adequate supplies to meet demand, traders said.
Kuwait was heard to be exporting one more than its usual export of two cargoes.
South Korean sellers were heard to have lowered offers to a slight discount on Tuesday, down from a 50-cents premium to Singapore spot quotes fob South Korea on Monday.
Chinese buyers were absent, traders said.
In the LSWR market, ample supplies were also weighing on levels.
Traders said South Korea was not expected to import any supplies in February as KEPCO, the state's utility company, has already imported its requirement.
Japan's February demand was expected to be weak as winter draws to an end. India and Italy were expected to import their usual 400,000 barrels and 600,000 barrels, traders said.
Malaysia was expected to export its normal 200,000-400,000 barrels in February.
Indonesia has allocated a total of 3.7 million barrels in February.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
